clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, her withdrawal to bed for weeks that first winter, Walter's distance from her in the orchard, his cutoff from his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and Glen's fights at the new school; by September 1953 June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, where the period settles.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: within months Walter drank heavily most nights, he and Glen blamed each other, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened, Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969, and Ida's heart trouble was found; by October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, where the period settles.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: within months Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours out of work, he and Marian had loud fights at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, she kept to her room and said little to her mother, Walter drank again after six years off it, and Nora's grandfather drank again; by June 1976 Nora was eating again and made the track team, where the period settles.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Hollis's mother Wilma selling her farm and moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990: within months Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, he took his mother's side, Nora's son Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flared on both hands, and Nora and Hollis had rows most nights; by June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, where the period settles.
